title: Essential finite type for a DVR with finite separable fraction extension
statement: Let $B,U$ be DVR domains [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring] and let $B\to U$ be a local ring map. Let $E/\operatorname{Frac}(B)$ be a finite separable field extension [def-pc-field-extension, def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], with compatible $B$- and $U$-algebra structures, and suppose $E=\operatorname{Frac}(U)$ via its specified structural map. Then $U$ is essentially of finite type over $B$ [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra]. No finiteness of $U$ as a $B$-module is assumed.

source.place: Tags 09E8 (normalized local DVRs, including the valuation-ring comparison) and 032L (finite separable normalization).

proof.text: Set C=integralClosure_B(E). Apply IsIntegralClosure.finite to make it a finite B-module. The integral-closure fraction-field theorem gives Frac(C)=E, and the Dedekind integral-closure instance makes C Dedekind.

Every element of C is integral over U by scalar extension, hence belongs to U because U is integrally closed in E. Codomain restriction to the range of U->E and its proved inverse construct C->U; the scalar tower over B is checked in E.

Contract m(U) to P in C. A base uniformizer belongs to P by locality and is nonzero by injectivity into E, so P is nonzero. The Mathlib Dedekind localization theorem makes S=C_P a DVR. Extend C->U to S->U and prove locality with the unit criterion for localization fractions.

Compatibility of C->S->E identifies E as Frac(S). Mathlib bijective_rangeRestrict_comp_of_valuationRing makes the local map S->U surjective. Composition makes S essentially of finite type over B, and EssFiniteType.of_surjective transfers that property to U.
